CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: Not applicable (prenatal)
Sample ID: [redacted ID]
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Sample Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal age: 35 years
Gestational age by ultrasound: 12 weeks
Indication for testing: Advanced maternal age, screening for Down syndrome and other chromosomal abnormalities
Sample type: Chorionic villus sample (CVS)

TEST PERFORMED
G-banded chromosome analysis (Karyotype)

METHODOLOGY
Chorionic villus cells were cultured according to standard protocols. Metaphase chromosomes were obtained from cultured cells and analyzed using G-banding technique at 400-550 band resolution. A minimum of 20 metaphase cells were examined, with detailed analysis of 5 cells and karyotyping of 2 cells.

RESULT
Karyotype: 46,XY

INTERPRETATION
G-banded chromosome analysis reveals a normal male karyotype (46,XY). No evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) or other numerical or structural chromosomal abnormalities was detected in the cells examined.

The normal male karyotype indicates:
- No evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome)
- No evidence of trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome)
- No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome)
- No evidence of sex chromosome abnormalities
- No evidence of unbalanced structural rearrangements detectable at this resolution

LIMITATIONS
This analysis cannot detect:
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements that do not result in gain or loss of chromosomal material
- Low-level mosaicism (<10%)
- Microdeletions or microduplications below the resolution of conventional cytogenetics
- Single gene disorders
- Uniparental disomy

CLINICAL CORRELATION
This result supersedes any previous rapid aneuploidy screening results (e.g., QF-PCR) performed on this pregnancy. The finding of a normal male karyotype is reassuring; however, this does not eliminate all genetic risks. The residual risk for chromosomal abnormalities is reduced to the background population risk.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss the results and any residual risks
2. Continue routine prenatal care and ultrasound monitoring
3. No indication for additional invasive testing based on these results
4. Consider non-invasive prenatal screening for other genetic conditions if clinically indicated

This report has been reviewed and authorized by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Cytogenetics Laboratory
License #: [redacted ID]
